data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's failure mode is installed as a causal prerequisite for the subject's own acceptance path, so that the subject is shaped to avoid the test's specific failure triggers instead of being measured by an independent observer. The 3-of-26 result arises because the shown-to-fail-first installation plants the failure signature into the acceptance ritual, and only those mutations whose guards directly mirror the planted failure signature are caught, while 23 of 26 mutations alter behaviour that the ritual never touches.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The test's subject was already shaped by prior constraints before the shown-to-fail installation, making the ritual a redundant re-statement","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 3-of-26 result is an artefact of mutation selection bias rather than a property of the installation mechanism","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A test constrains its subject whenever it is a necessary condition for acceptance, regardless of installation order, so 'shown-to-fail-first' is confounded with ordinary acceptance testing","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'shown-to-fail-first' installation converts a descriptive check into a normative boundary condition. When the author must first observe a specific failure before the guard is admitted, the guard becomes an instrument of the ritual's registry rather than a property of the subject. Mutations that modify the same code path as the planted failure are constrained (caught), while mutations in adjacent or structurally similar paths are described (observed but not blocked), producing the 3/26 distribution.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
